doc.title: Herbie Hancock interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, November 18, 1995

title: Donald Byrd brings him to New York
summary: Byrd was roommate and big brother, got him his first record and publishing company, and introduced him to Miles.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Let me make a quantum there ‘cause I want to hook in on something that you said. You said the kids that you were hanging out with who were the hippest, the most mature and the most mysterious that’s what turned you on. So now from your entrance into jazz to the place where you would be asked to play keyboard with the hippest most mysterious man in all of jazz. You know we’re talking about Miles. Tell us about how you got to work with Miles and how that liaison came about and some of the dynamics in there.

All right. I was brought to New York from Chicago by Donald Byrd, another great trumpeter. And Donald really took me under his wing and we shared an apartment together, he was my roommate and he was like really a big brother to me. And he really showed me the ropes in New York and he really encouraged me in so many ways and taught me a lot of things. And was the person responsible for me doing my very first record as a leader. He is responsible for me getting my own publishing company so that my first tunes were published in my own company, and not in the record company’s company. Thank goodness for that because one of the first tunes I wrote was “Watermelon Man.”
It’s still played today. And he was also responsible for introducing me to Miles Davis. So I owe a lot to Donald Byrd. I mean so much that I could never repay him for what he’s done for me.
